What I changed in Change Stack

CodeRabbit Change Stack · Formbricks #8650 · Parth Pawar

I chose one review task: check a summary against the code, inspect the access guard, then return without losing my place. I kept CodeRabbit’s layer-based model, summary jumps and deliberate viewed state. M changes how those pieces work together.

What I focused onDecision and reason
Keep the file and review scope visible.The rail keeps file navigation available. This file and Entire layer make the context scope explicit. File controls stay beside the diff; secondary tools sit behind a disclosure. This keeps the reading task visible while moving through the PR.
Make each summary point checkable.Six compact rows link statements to specific code ranges. The full source wording and Whole function stay available. About links explains the manual mapping. A highlight helps locate code; the reviewer still has to judge the claim.
Return from the guard without rebuilding context.Inspect guard opens feedback-access.ts. Return restores the caller’s statement, reading position and context. I built one route to demonstrate continuity across files. Automatic dependency navigation remains outside this prototype.
Keep progress separate from approval.Opening a file marks nothing viewed. Mark viewed has Undo. The layer distinguishes seven reviewable files from two unavailable patches. Summary seen is separate, and Submit review is disabled for this merged PR.

The space tradeoff

Wrapped 13 px code avoids horizontal movement but adds vertical scrolling. Added-file Split gives the empty Before pane 96 px; Equal panes restores 50/50. Compact statement rows keep all six checks visible at 1280 × 720. Modified-file Split still needs a separate check.

What I checked

I checked the caller/guard return, statement links, viewed/Undo and layouts at 1440, 1280 and 1100 px. Targeted keyboard checks cover current-range state, focus and Escape. Developer comprehension and a full screen-reader audit still need testing.

What I’d test next

I’d compare the same task on both screens, then ask developers to start from code and challenge the summary. Watch explanation accuracy, missed branches and backtracking. Precise links are only useful if people still inspect enough code.
